content.content:
Haj-Wan: "I wait for Sei-Wan, my kin. He walked out into the basin alone, to prove himself to the Agaceph, and he has not come back. I am Agaceph too. By our custom none of us may follow a walk-out, so I stay at this gate. An outsider may follow him. He went east from the gate through the shallows, and he is up among the roots there. Vipers lie in the roots, and the mud holds anyone who stands still. Nothing that walks in the basin lives long. Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden beside me, will say the same. I want him alive. He wants the walk-out to count, and it counts only if he comes home on his own feet. If another brings him in, the Agaceph will say he did not finish. I would have him alive and shamed sooner than proud and dead. Bring him home if you must. But if he can walk, let the walk-out be his own."
Quest started: The Gates of Helstrom
Journal entry (The Gates of Helstrom): Haj-Wan, waiting beside Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden at Helstrom's gate, told me her kin Sei-Wan walked out into the basin alone to prove himself to his tribe, the Agaceph. He has not come back. By their custom the Agaceph may not follow him, but an outsider may. He went east from the gate through the shallows. I'm to find him up among the roots there.
New objective: Find Sei-Wan in the shallows east of Helstrom's gate.
Topics:
  1. What are you waiting for here?

content.text:
I finished the one quest the game offered, "The Gates of Helstrom", and gave my take. The journal has no active objectives left.

Haj-Wan's kinsman Sei-Wan had walked out into the basin to prove himself and not come back. I found him stuck up in the roots, with a viper between him and the gate. I killed the viper. Then I told him to walk home on his own feet and said nothing to Haj-Wan, so his walk-out stays his own. The cost is that Haj-Wan keeps waiting at the gate without knowing he's safe.

In my take I said the quest was short and clear, and the choice at the end felt like a real one. The warden's generic dialogue was repetitive. I'd like to see what comes next, such as the Dwemer ruins or the boat captain Sells-Dear, but nothing further was offered.
